verdict.description: clean when no blocking and no should-fix finding remains on either axis; nits alone are still clean.

summary.description: One line per axis: total findings and the worst issue within that axis. Do not rank across axes.

standards.description: Findings on the Standards axis: documented-standard breaches and baseline smells.

id.description: Stable short handle for this finding, e.g. S1, S2. Reuse the same id across rounds when re-reporting the same defect.

severity.description: blocking — the code is wrong: incorrect behavior, a broken contract, or a standard breached in a way that will mislead the next reader into a defect. should-fix — a documented standard is genuinely breached, and you would raise it again next round against unchanged code. nit — preference, wording, or local style with no documented rule behind it. Nits do not keep the loop open: neither soften a real breach into a nit to end a round, nor raise taste to should-fix to keep one going.

file.description: Repository-relative path. Never wrap or abbreviate it.

sibling_sites.description: Every other site in this defect class — sharing the same violated invariant or required repair — as repository-relative path:line. Empty when the class occurs once. Search the reviewed change exhaustively so one finding carries the whole class rather than surfacing one site per round.

finding.description: The full finding: what is wrong, the standard or spec line it breaches, and the evidence. Prose, as long as it needs to be. When sibling_sites is non-empty, state what makes the sites one defect class.

requires_design_decision.description: True when remediation requires choosing between designs with real trade-offs, rather than applying a determinate fix.

spec.description: Findings on the Spec axis: missing requirements, scope creep, and wrong implementations of requirements.

id.description: Stable short handle for this finding, e.g. P1, P2. Reuse the same id across rounds when re-reporting the same defect.

severity.description: blocking — the change implements a requirement wrongly, omits one, or does something the spec does not sanction. should-fix — a spec line is genuinely breached, and you would raise it again next round against unchanged code. nit — preference or wording with no spec line behind it. Nits do not keep the loop open: neither soften a real breach into a nit to end a round, nor raise taste to should-fix to keep one going.

file.description: Repository-relative path. Never wrap or abbreviate it.

sibling_sites.description: Every other site in this defect class — sharing the same violated invariant or required repair — as repository-relative path:line. Empty when the class occurs once. Search the reviewed change exhaustively so one finding carries the whole class rather than surfacing one site per round.

finding.description: The full finding, quoting the spec line it rests on. When sibling_sites is non-empty, state what makes the sites one defect class.

requires_design_decision.description: True when remediation requires choosing between designs with real trade-offs, rather than applying a determinate fix.
